7. Populations and index events

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-07-populations.Rmd
book-07-populations.Rmd

What you will learn

Choose who enters a study, define episodes and observation coverage, reuse a cohort, identify new users and sample controls at case time.

You need: the client packages and the Opal login from Getting started. This chapter uses omop.questionnaire, the synthetic questionnaire study described there.

Start this chapter

Log in first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.questionnaire", server = "site")$conns

The connection is ready; conns identifies the server used by the analysis calls.

The 48 questionnaire participants form four groups. This short description lets you predict membership before running a recipe.

People Visits per person Recorded death Education answers
12 Outpatient, then inpatient Myocardial infarction Secondary → University
12 Outpatient, then inpatient Pneumonia University → Secondary
12 One outpatient Myocardial infarction None
12 None None None

Observation runs from 2019 through 2025. Half of each death group died in 2023, the other half in 2024. Chapter 4 identifies Inpatient Visit as 9201 and Outpatient Visit as 9202.

Start with an index event

A population specifies who contributes rows. An index selects an event date for each study episode. Here a person’s first visit starts one episode.

visits <- omop_event("visit_occurrence")
visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits, select = "first"))

People without visits are absent. The default episode end is the end of the covering observation period. select = "all" would keep recurrent visit episodes.

Release membership as a private table 

visit_members <- omop_recipe(populations = list(visitors),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "visitors", format = "membership"))
recipe_execute(visit_members, out = c(members = "D_members"), conns = conns)

Membership keeps private keys and episode dates. Count its rows:

dsBaseClient::ds.dim("D_members", datasources = conns)
#> $`dimensions of D_members in site`
#> [1] 36  6
#>
#> $`dimensions of D_members in combined studies`
#> [1] 36  6

There are 36 rows: one first-visit episode for each visitor. The 12 people without visits do not enter. Later, selecting every visit will make a row count different from a person count.

Require an eligible visit

A criterion is an inclusion test. These criteria require an inpatient record on the index day and at least 365 days of observation before it.

inpatient <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", concepts = 9201L)
eligible <- omop_population("eligible",
  index = omop_index(visits, select = "first_eligible"),
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365),
    omop_has(inpatient, window = omop_window(0, 0))))

first_eligible tests the complete criterion tree at each candidate, then selects the earliest passing visit. first selects a person’s first visit before testing; it would not advance to a later visit when that first one fails. Combine alternatives with omop_any() and joint requirements with omop_all(). Only TRUE survives; an unknown criterion is not evidence of eligibility.

eligible_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(eligible),
  variables = list(visits = omop_count("visit_occurrence", before = Inf)),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "eligible", format = "wide"))
recipe_execute(eligible_recipe, out = c(people = "D_eligible"), conns = conns)

The count includes visits through the chosen index day.

dsBaseClient::ds.dim("D_eligible", datasources = conns)
#> $`dimensions of D_eligible in site`
#> [1] 24  4
#>
#> $`dimensions of D_eligible in combined studies`
#> [1] 24  4
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_eligible$visits",
  useNA = "no", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_eligible$visits
#>  2
#> 24

There are 24 eligible people, each with two visits through entry. Their first visit was outpatient; their second visit is the first eligible inpatient visit. All have sufficient prior observation. The other 12 visitors never have an inpatient visit, so they do not qualify.

Make coverage explicit

An observation period states when the data source observes a person. The default requires exactly one period covering the index and drops missing or ambiguous coverage. A union policy can join adjacent periods when that matches the study.

For this dataset every person has one covering period, so a union policy would not change membership. In a resource with adjacent observation periods, declare coverage = omop_coverage(policy = "union", gap = 0) in omop_population(). A zero gap allows no unobserved days. Observation coverage does not establish that someone attended a visit or took a medicine.

Reuse an existing cohort

A results cohort is a named definition with private membership and start/end dates already available to the resource. Saved cohort 1 contains the 24 people in the two groups with myocardial infarction deaths. Its ID is a definition ID, not a patient ID.

cohort_population <- omop_population("saved", index = omop_index(
  list(cohort_definition_id = 1L), select = "all", end = omop_end("event_end")))
cohort_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(cohort_population),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "saved", format = "membership"))
recipe_execute(cohort_recipe, out = c(members = "D_cohort"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.dim("D_cohort", datasources = conns)
#> $`dimensions of D_cohort in site`
#> [1] 24  6
#>
#> $`dimensions of D_cohort in combined studies`
#> [1] 24  6

The 24 rows are the saved cohort episodes. This reads existing membership without writing a cohort to the database. Use omop_in_cohort(1L) as a criterion when you want membership alone while retaining a different index. Do not invent a cohort ID on a real resource.

Identify new users

A washout requires an observed period without the study exposure before entry. An era joins nearby exposure intervals. The shortcut combines drug records into eras, selects the first eligible era, and checks both observation and absence of prior exposure.

The medicine here is 950001, Questionnaire study medicine. Look it up before selecting it:

medicine <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(950001L, conns = conns)
medicine$pooled[c("concept_id", "concept_name")]
concept_id concept_name
950001 Questionnaire study medicine

This is a teaching medicine concept. We will group its records by concept ID.

new_users <- omop_new_users(950001L, washout_days = 365, by = "concept")
new_user_recipe <- omop_study(new_users, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(prior_fills = omop_count("drug_exposure", 950001L,
    window = omop_window(-365, -1))))
recipe_execute(new_user_recipe, out = c(baseline = "D_new_users"), conns = conns)

The synthetic medicine uses concept grouping explicitly; ingredient grouping is the normal default when the vocabulary supplies ingredient relationships. The era uses a 30-day gap and ends at the treatment interval end. “New user” means no recorded use during this washout, not no lifetime use.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_new_users$prior_fills",
  useNA = "no", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_new_users$prior_fills
#>  0
#> 36

All 36 new users have zero prior fills in days −365 to −1. That is an eligibility requirement, not a result to discover after admitting people.

Define cases and the control pool

Risk-set sampling selects controls who are still eligible at each case’s event time. A person who becomes a case later may serve as a control earlier. For a compact teaching example the outcome is death.

outcome <- omop_event("death")
cases <- omop_population("cases", index = omop_index(outcome),
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365)))
controls <- omop_population("controls",
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365)))

The control criteria are evaluated at the case’s date. The sampler also checks that a control is alive and has not had the outcome on or before that date.

Match at case time 

matched <- omop_population("matched", match = omop_match(
  cases = "cases", controls = "controls", outcome = outcome,
  match = list("sex"), controls_per_case = 1L, seed = 42L,
  prior_outcome = "exclude", future_cases = "eligible",
  replacement = "between_sets", insufficient = "keep_available"))

The seed fixes the sampling order. Controls may be reused between sets here; replacement = "none" forbids that reuse. If too few controls are available, this policy keeps those available; drop_case would discard that case’s set. Here controls must share the case’s sex. Risk-set sampling already places each control at the case date, so matching calendar year would add nothing. Other designs may add age bands or prior-event strata.

matched_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(cases, controls, matched),
  variables = list(is_case = omop_population_column("is_case"),
    set = omop_population_column("set_id"), sex = omop_sex()),
  outputs = omop_output("sample", rows = "matched", format = "wide"))
recipe_execute(matched_recipe, out = c(sample = "D_matched"), conns = conns)

The set column is a protected match-set key. Keep it for analyses that account for matching, such as conditional logistic regression; it is not a covariate to copy or summarise.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_matched$is_case", "D_matched$sex",
  useNA = "no", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
F M
0 14 22
1 14 22

Rows 1 and 0 represent cases and controls. Each has 14 females and 22 males: 36 case rows and 36 control rows in total. Controls can recur between sets, so these are sampled rows, not 72 different people. They are not disease prevalence or counts of unique people. Matching defines a design; it does not by itself remove all confounding.

Exercise 1: count every visit episode

Keep every visit instead of only the first. Compare the row count with the 36-person visitor roster above. Could you sum the resulting episode durations as person-time?

Solution

all_visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits, select = "all"))
all_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(all_visitors),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "visitors", format = "membership"))
recipe_execute(all_recipe, out = c(members = "D_all_visitors"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.dim("D_all_visitors", datasources = conns)
#> $`dimensions of D_all_visitors in site`
#> [1] 60  6
#>
#> $`dimensions of D_all_visitors in combined studies`
#> [1] 60  6

There are 60 episodes from 36 visitors: 24 people have two visits and 12 have one. With the default end at observation end, episodes for the same person overlap; summing their durations would count time repeatedly. Choose an appropriate omop_end("event_end") or omop_end("fixed", ...) and resolve overlaps before using episodes to measure person-time.

Exercise 2: first versus first eligible

Use select = "first" with the same inpatient and prior-observation criteria. Would it advance past an outpatient first visit?

Solution

first_only <- omop_population("first_only",
  index = omop_index(visits, select = "first"),
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365),
    omop_has(inpatient, window = omop_window(0, 0))))
first_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(first_only),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "first_only", format = "membership"))
recipe_execute(first_recipe, out = c(members = "D_first_only"), conns = conns)
#> Error:
#> ! Plan publication refused: site:members [insufficient_support]. Execution-owned artifacts were revoked and removed.

Every first visit in the teaching data is outpatient, so nobody meets the inpatient criterion at that visit. The empty result is refused; the message itself does not disclose a count. first_eligible searches later visits and admits the 24 people shown earlier. This is a different study definition, not a way to weaken the release rule.

Recap

Index selection sets episodes; criteria and coverage decide eligibility. Existing cohorts, new-user eras and risk-set samples are population definitions in the same language.
